_source: Compiled 2026-09-13 from MDWFP, Outdoor Alabama, GA DNR/GON and local fishing records.
_note: Weight ranges are typical rod-and-reel catches, not state records. Trophy is the threshold for the NEW PERSONAL BEST fanfare.

krebs_lake.water: brackish oxbow of the Pascagoula, formerly Lake Catahoula
krebs_lake.landmark: LaPointe-Krebs House, built c.1757 - oldest standing building in Mississippi

species.name: Red Drum
species.note: Tailing on the flats at low light.

species.name: Black Drum
species.note: Bottom feeder. Slow and heavy.

species.name: Speckled Trout
species.note: Around dock lights after dark.

species.name: Bluegill
species.note: Off the docks. The first fish anyone catches here.

species.name: Channel Catfish
species.note: Works the bottom all night.

pascagoula_river.water: largest undammed river in the contiguous US - 80 miles, Leaf and Chickasawhay confluence to the Gulf
pascagoula_river.special_mechanic: SALT LEDGE - the fresh/salt boundary slides with the tide. In late summer it can sit a few miles north of the I-10 bridge. Species available depend on which side the boat is on.

species.name: Largemouth Bass
species.note: FRESH side. Cypress knees and laydowns. 12-inch minimum, 10 fish.

species.name: Bluegill
species.note: FRESH side. Sloughs and backwater.

species.name: Flathead Catfish
species.note: FRESH side. Live bait only. Most prized of the three cats.

species.name: Blue Catfish
species.note: FRESH side. Middle river, around the bluffs.

species.name: Channel Catfish
species.note: FRESH side.

species.name: Longnose Gar
species.note: FRESH side. Rolls on the surface. Hard to hook, unmistakable.

species.name: Redfish
species.note: SALT side. Marsh drains and tide rips.

species.name: Speckled Trout
species.note: SALT side. Grass flats, current edges.

species.name: Southern Flounder
species.note: SALT side. Flat on the bottom, ambushes.

escatawpa_river.location: George/Jackson Co. MS and Mobile/Washington Co. AL
escatawpa_river.water: 129-mile blackwater tributary of the Pascagoula. Tannin-stained, tea-coloured, white sand bars. Drops about one foot per mile.
escatawpa_river.name_origin: Choctaw Uska-a-Topa, roughly 'where cane is cut' - rivercane

species.name: Largemouth Bass
species.note: Dark lures against dark water. Work the cypress roots.

species.name: Chain Pickerel
species.note: Ambush predator in the weed edges. Fast and toothy.

species.name: Longear Sunfish
species.note: Small but the most vividly coloured fish in the game. Orange and electric blue.

species.name: Longnose Gar
species.note: Sunning in the shallows over the white sand.

species.name: Channel Catfish
species.note: Deep holes on the outside bends.

species.name: Striped Bass
species.note: Runs up from the bay.

species.name: Redfish
species.note: Lower reaches only, where it goes brackish fast.

lake_lanier.water: 38,000-acre Army Corps reservoir on the upper Chattahoochee, ~50 miles NE of Atlanta. Deep and clear.
lake_lanier.structure: Standing timber - the forest was flooded when the lake was impounded and is still down there. Plus roadbeds, rock humps, brushpiles, sunk boats.
lake_lanier.special_mechanic: SONAR - chunky 1997-style fish finder strip showing bottom contour and fish arcs. This is the map where depth matters.

species.name: Spotted Bass
species.note: THE fish here. Widely called the best spotted bass lake in the country. Holds in the top limbs of drowned trees.

species.name: Striped Bass
best_lures: live herring on a planer board
species.note: Suspends in submerged timber next to the river channel. Lake record 47 lb.

species.name: Largemouth Bass
species.note: Submerged timber in the creeks. Lake record 17 lb 9 oz.

species.name: Black Crappie
species.note: Brushpiles. Goes deep in summer heat.

species.name: Channel Catfish
species.note: Deep flats.
